title: How to Know If a Territory Program Is Right for Your Contracting Business — Five Questions
content:
### **Question 1 — Do You Serve a Definable Geography?** 

Territory programs work when your service area can be defined in ZIP codes. If you serve specific suburbs — Wilmette, Cedarburg, the Lake Country corridor — territory presence concentrates your recognition where your trucks already go. If your work is scattered across three counties with no pattern, route density comes first. 

###  **Question 2 — Can You Follow Up on Inspection Requests Quickly?** 

SIT GroundForce™ generates inspection requests through direct homeowner conversations and personal follow-up notes. Those requests convert when your team responds within a day. If your follow-up process is inconsistent, fix that before investing in any lead-generating channel — territory or otherwise. 

 **Question 3 — Are You Building for Next Year, Not Just Next Month?** 

Territory presence compounds over months. Contractors who need revenue in two weeks should not start here. Contractors building a durable position in specific suburbs — the kind that produces inbound calls year after year — are exactly who the model serves.

 **Question 4 — Does Category Exclusivity Matter to You?** 

One approved partner per industry per territory means the recognition you build belongs to your brand alone. If you have watched shared-lead services sell the same homeowner to four competitors, you already understand why this matters. 

 **Question 5 — Do You Want to Test Before You Commit?** 

Every SIT™ partnership can begin with a Visibility Pilot — a structured evaluation phase with weekly prepayment, one-week notice, and a results review at the end. Low commitment, measurable from the first week.
